trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Barcelona
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 13:00. Use travel time to rest.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Barcelona Airport around 13:00. Take the Aerobus (€5.90) or Metro L9 Sud (€5.15) to the city center. Check in to Barcelona Boutique Stay in Eixample. Once settled, take a self-guided walk along Passeig de Gràcia to admire the famous 'Block of Discord' — spot Casa Batlló, Casa Amatller, and Casa Lleó Morera from the outside for free. Marvel at Gaudí's iconic facades without spending a cent.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll through the Eixample grid streets and explore the lively Gaixample neighborhood. Head to Carrer del Consell de Cent or Carrer de Muntaner for pre-dinner drinks at a local bar. Many bars offer free tapas with a drink during happy hour. End the night at a low-key neighborhood bar or terrace to soak in the Barcelona atmosphere and recover from travel.

meals.breakfast: Grab a coffee and croissant at the airport or a café near the hotel upon arrival — budget €3–5.
meals.lunch: Pick up a fresh bocadillo (sandwich) or slice of pizza from a local bakery or takeaway near Passeig de Gràcia — budget €4–6.
meals.dinner: Try a Menú del Día (set menu) at a local restaurant in Eixample — typically includes starter, main, dessert, and drink for €12–15. Look for spots on side streets away from tourist areas.

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 is intentionally light due to afternoon arrival. Get your bearings, pick up a T-Casual metro card (10 trips for ~€11.35) at any metro station — it will save money throughout the trip. Stay hydrated; August in Barcelona can be very hot.

day_by_day.morning: Start early with a visit to the Sagrada Família (book tickets online in advance — €26 for basic entry, €36 with tower access). Arrive when it opens at 9:00 to beat the crowds and the midday heat. Spend 1.5–2 hours exploring Gaudí's unfinished masterpiece, the most iconic piece of architecture in Barcelona. Afterward, walk through the surrounding Gaudí-designed streetscape.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Park Güell (book timed entry tickets in advance — €10 for the Monumental Zone, or explore the free outer areas). Spend time admiring the mosaic terraces, Gingerbread Houses, and panoramic views over the city. Walk back downhill through Gràcia neighborhood — a bohemian, artsy district full of independent shops and plazas. Browse the local market at Mercat de l'Abaceria if open.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Eixample to freshen up. Head out for Barcelona's famous nightlife — start with bar-hopping in the Eixample district. Many bars don't get busy until 22:00–23:00. Look for free-entry bars with cheap cañas (small beers, €2–3 each). If you want a club experience, check out Sala Apolo or Razzmatazz (entry €10–15, often includes a drink).

meals.breakfast: Café amb llet (coffee with milk) and a pa amb tomàquet (bread with tomato) at a local bar near the hotel — budget €3–5.
meals.lunch: Grab a bocadillo or empanada from a bakery near Park Güell, or eat at a casual café in Gràcia — budget €6–9.
meals.dinner: Menú del Día at a restaurant in Gràcia or Eixample — budget €12–15. Alternatively, buy fresh produce and cured meats from a local supermarket (Mercadona or Lidl) for a picnic-style meal — budget €5–8.

day_by_day.notes: Book Sagrada Família and Park Güell tickets online well in advance — they sell out fast, especially in August. Wear comfortable walking shoes and bring water. The free outer zone of Park Güell is still worth visiting if you want to save the €10 entry fee.

day_by_day.morning: Take the metro to the Gothic Quarter (Barri Gòtic) — one of the best free architectural experiences in Barcelona. Wander the labyrinthine medieval streets and discover the Barcelona Cathedral (free entry before 12:30 and after 17:30 on weekdays). Visit the Plaça de Sant Jaume, Pont del Bisbe (the neo-Gothic bridge), and the ancient Roman ruins visible through glass floors in the streets. Explore the Plaça Reial with its Gaudí-designed lampposts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to El Born neighborhood, adjacent to the Gothic Quarter. Visit the Basílica de Santa Maria del Mar — a stunning 14th-century Gothic church with free entry (donations welcome). Explore the Born Cultural Centre (€6 entry, or free on Sunday afternoons after 15:00) to see the excavated medieval ruins beneath a stunning iron-and-glass structure. Browse the boutiques and street art of El Born.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Barceloneta beach for a sunset walk — it's free and beautiful in August. Watch the sun dip behind the city skyline. Afterward, explore the beachfront bars (chiringuitos) for a drink. Return to Eixample or stay in El Born for dinner, then explore the nightlife in El Born and El Raval — both neighborhoods have affordable bars and live music venues.

meals.breakfast: Churros con chocolate at a traditional café in the Gothic Quarter — budget €4–6.
meals.lunch: Mercat de la Boqueria on La Rambla is touristy but fun to browse; grab fresh fruit or a snack. For a real budget meal, eat at the market bar counters — budget €8–12. Alternatively, Mercat de Santa Caterina in El Born is less crowded and cheaper.
meals.dinner: Tapas and pintxos bar-hopping in El Born — order patatas bravas, croquetas, and pan con tomate. Budget €10–14 for a satisfying spread with drinks.

day_by_day.notes: Avoid La Rambla at night — it's known for pickpockets. Keep bags close in the Gothic Quarter and on the metro. The Gothic Quarter is best explored on foot; get lost intentionally — every corner reveals something beautiful.

day_by_day.morning: Take the metro or a bus up to Montjuïc hill. Visit the Fundació Joan Miró (€14 entry) — a world-class modern art museum in a stunning rationalist building designed by Josep Lluís Sert. Alternatively, if saving money, skip inside and explore the outdoor sculptures and terraces for free. Walk up to the Castell de Montjuïc (€5 entry or free on Sundays after 15:00) for sweeping panoramic views of Barcelona, the port, and the Mediterranean.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk or take the cable car (Telefèric de Montjuïc, €12.70 round trip) back down to the city. Head to the Poble Sec neighborhood at the foot of Montjuïc — a hip, local area with great street art and affordable eateries. Visit the Pavelló Mies van der Rohe (€7 entry) — a reconstructed modernist masterpiece from the 1929 World Exposition, essential for architecture lovers. Stroll through the Parc de Joan Miró nearby for free.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Eixample and explore the Esquerra de l'Eixample (left side of Eixample) — known for its vibrant LGBTQ+ scene and buzzing nightlife. The area around Carrer del Consell de Cent, Carrer de Muntaner, and Carrer de Casanova has dozens of bars and clubs. Many venues offer free entry before midnight. Try a craft beer bar or a cocktail bar with happy hour deals (cocktails from €6–8).

meals.breakfast: Fresh orange juice and a croissant from a local café in Eixample before heading out — budget €3–5.
meals.lunch: Eat at a casual restaurant in Poble Sec — the area has excellent value Menú del Día options — budget €11–14. Carrer de Blai (the 'pintxos street') is nearby and perfect for cheap bites — pintxos from €1.50–2.50 each.
meals.dinner: Cook a simple meal using ingredients from a local supermarket, or grab takeaway falafel or kebab near the hotel — budget €5–8. Save money tonight for drinks on a big night out.

day_by_day.notes: Montjuïc is very hot in August — go early and bring plenty of water and sunscreen. The free bus (Bus Turístic) can be expensive; use public buses instead (Bus 55 goes up to Montjuïc from Paral·lel metro station). Carrer de Blai pintxos bars are best visited around 19:00–21:00 when they're freshest.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Palau de la Música Catalana in El Born — a stunning UNESCO World Heritage modernista concert hall designed by Lluís Domènech i Montaner (guided tours €22, or attend a morning concert for a more affordable and immersive experience, tickets from €15). Even viewing the exterior facade and the stained-glass lantern from outside is breathtaking and free. Afterward, walk along Via Laietana and back through the Gothic Quarter one last time.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the Diagonal or Gràcia area for some last-minute souvenir shopping at local markets or independent shops — avoid tourist trap shops on La Rambla. Visit the Mercat de l'Abaceria (Mercat de Gràcia) for unique local goods. Take a final walk along Passeig de Gràcia and revisit your favorite spots. If time allows, visit the free rooftop terrace of El Corte Inglés department store on Plaça de Catalunya for great city views.
day_by_day.evening: Depending on your departure time, enjoy a final farewell dinner in Eixample. Splurge slightly on your last night with a nicer sit-down meal — try traditional Catalan cuisine (escudella, fideuà, crema catalana) at a mid-range restaurant — budget €18–25. Take a final stroll through the illuminated streets of Eixample, admiring the modernista architecture lit up at night. Head to the airport via Aerobus or Metro L9.

meals.breakfast: Full Spanish breakfast at a local bar — café con leche, tostada con tomate y aceite, and fresh orange juice — budget €5–7.
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a café or grab takeaway from a local market — budget €7–10. Keep it light if you plan a bigger farewell dinner.
meals.dinner: Farewell Catalan dinner at a traditional restaurant in Eixample. Look for spots recommended on Google Maps with high ratings and reasonable prices — budget €18–25 including a glass of local wine or cava.

day_by_day.notes: Check your flight departure time and factor in travel to the airport (Aerobus takes ~35 minutes from Plaça de Catalunya, runs every 5–10 minutes). Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before departure. Store luggage at the hotel until departure if checking out early. August is peak season — book airport transport in advance if possible.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival & Hotel Check-In — Flight LH lands at 13:00, so no morning activities. Take the Aerobus or Metro L9 Sud from El Prat Airport to Eixample (approx. 35–45 min). Check in to Barcelona Boutique Stay, freshen up, and get oriented in the neighborhood.
day_by_day.afternoon: Eixample Neighborhood Stroll & First Impressions — After settling in, take a leisurely walk along Passeig de Gràcia to admire the famous 'Block of Discord': Casa Batlló, Casa Amatller, and Casa Lleó Morera from the outside. Window-shop and soak in the Eixample grid architecture. Pick up a city map and book timed tickets for upcoming attractions online.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner & Gentle First Night Out — Head to the Eixample bar scene for a relaxed introduction. Grab pre-dinner vermouth (vermut) at a classic local bar, then enjoy dinner at a mid-range restaurant nearby.

meals.breakfast: Skip or grab a coffee and croissant at the airport or a café near the hotel upon arrival.
meals.lunch: Light bite near the hotel — try a bocadillo (Spanish sandwich) or a menú del día (set lunch menu) at a local Eixample café for around €12–15.
meals.dinner: Cervecería Catalana on Carrer de Mallorca — beloved local spot serving excellent tapas and pintxos. Expect €25–35 per person with drinks.

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 is intentionally light given the early afternoon arrival. Use this evening to book timed-entry tickets online for Sagrada Família (Day 2) and Park Güell (Day 3) if not already done — they sell out fast in August.

day_by_day.morning: Gothic Quarter & El Born Architecture Walk — Start the day with a self-guided or small-group walking tour through the medieval Gothic Quarter. Explore the Barcelona Cathedral, Plaça Reial, Pont del Bisbe, and the Roman ruins visible through glass floors. Cross into El Born to see the Basílica de Santa Maria del Mar and the trendy boutique streets. Allow 2.5–3 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Sagrada Família Guided Tour — Head to Gaudí's iconic basilica for your pre-booked afternoon guided tour (book the 14:30 or 15:00 slot). The skip-the-line guided tour covers the nave, apse, towers (if included), and the museum below. Budget 2–2.5 hours. Afterward, walk around the exterior to appreciate the Nativity and Passion facades.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in Eixample & Early Nightlife Preview — Return to Eixample for dinner, then take a first dip into the neighborhood's nightlife with cocktails at a rooftop bar.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a nearby bakery — try a café amb llet (coffee with milk) and pa amb tomàquet (bread with tomato) at a local bar for €5–8.
meals.lunch: El Born neighborhood — Bar del Pla on Carrer de la Montcada offers excellent Catalan tapas at mid-range prices (€15–20 per person).
meals.dinner: Parking Pizza on Londres Street in Eixample — creative, quality pizzas in a cool setting, great value at €18–25 per person. Or try Bodega Sepúlveda for Catalan wine and charcuterie boards.

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes for the Gothic Quarter — cobblestones can be tough. The Sagrada Família is extremely popular in August; arriving at your timed slot exactly is important. Keep your ticket QR code accessible.

day_by_day.morning: Park Güell & Gràcia Neighborhood Exploration — Take the Metro or a taxi to Park Güell for your timed entry (book the 09:00 or 10:00 slot to beat the midday heat). Explore Gaudí's colorful mosaic terraces, the Hypostyle Room, and the winding paths with panoramic city views. Allow 1.5–2 hours inside the monumental zone, then explore the free surrounding park.
day_by_day.afternoon: Gràcia Neighborhood Wander — Descend from Park Güell into the charming Gràcia district on foot. Explore Plaça del Sol, Plaça de la Vila de Gràcia, and the bohemian streets lined with independent shops and cafés. Visit Casa Vicens (Gaudí's first major work) — a hidden gem with far fewer crowds than his other works.
day_by_day.evening: Eixample Nightlife & Cocktail Bar Crawl — This is the night for the famous Eixample (Gayxample) nightlife experience. Start with craft cocktails at Dry Martini Bar on Carrer d'Aribau (an iconic Barcelona institution), then move to a second cocktail bar, and finish the night at one of the area's popular clubs or late-night bars.

meals.breakfast: Grab breakfast before heading out — Federal Café in Sant Antoni (nearby Eixample) is a beloved brunch spot with excellent coffee and avocado toast for €10–14.
meals.lunch: Gràcia neighborhood — La Pepita on Carrer de Còrsega serves creative montaditos (small open-faced sandwiches) at great value, around €15–20 per person.
meals.dinner: Pre-nightlife dinner at Parking Pizza or Morro Fi vermouth bar in Eixample for light tapas and natural wine (€20–28 per person) — keep it lighter before the bar crawl.

day_by_day.notes: August in Barcelona means Park Güell is extremely hot by midday — the early morning slot is strongly recommended. Bring water and sunscreen. For the nightlife crawl, Barcelona's scene starts late: dinner around 21:00, first bar around 23:00, clubs from 01:00 onward. Pace yourself!

day_by_day.morning: Relaxed Morning Recovery — After the late night, allow a slow morning. Sleep in, enjoy a leisurely breakfast, and stroll through the Sant Antoni Market (Mercat de Sant Antoni) near Eixample for fresh produce, books, and local atmosphere. Browse the Sunday book market stalls (open weekday mornings too in summer).
day_by_day.afternoon: Barceloneta Beach & Seafood Lunch — Take the Metro L4 (Yellow Line) to Barceloneta station. Spend 2–3 hours relaxing on the beach, swimming in the Mediterranean. Rent a sun lounger (€6–10) for comfort. After the beach, walk along the Passeig Marítim promenade and enjoy a long, leisurely seafood lunch at a beachside restaurant.
day_by_day.evening: El Born Evening & Cocktails — Head back to the El Born neighborhood for a more relaxed evening. Explore its cocktail bars and wine bars, then enjoy a final nightcap at a rooftop bar with city views.

meals.breakfast: Slow brunch at Federal Café or Cosmo Café in Eixample — eggs, coffee, juice for €12–16.
meals.lunch: Barceloneta seafood — La Cova Fumada (cash only, arrive early as it closes when food runs out) for authentic bombes and seafood, or La Mar Salada on Passeig de Joan de Borbó for a sit-down fresh seafood paella or grilled fish (€30–40 per person — a worthy mid-range splurge).
meals.dinner: El Born — Bar del Convent in the courtyard of the Convent de Sant Agustí for light evening tapas and wine in a magical setting (€18–25 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Barceloneta Beach is very crowded in August — arrive by 14:00 after lunch to find space, or go early. Watch your belongings on the beach (petty theft is common in tourist areas). La Cova Fumada is legendary but tiny — arrive right when it opens.

day_by_day.morning: Palau de la Música Catalana & Final Architecture Gems — Start the final day with a guided tour of the Palau de la Música Catalana (book in advance), a stunning UNESCO-listed Modernista concert hall by Lluís Domènech i Montaner — Gaudí's great rival. The interior is breathtaking, especially with morning light through the stained-glass skylight. Afterward, walk to the nearby Arc de Triomf and Ciutadella Park.
day_by_day.afternoon: Montjuïc & Poble Sec — Take the cable car or bus up to Montjuïc for panoramic views of the city and port. Visit the Fundació Joan Miró (mid-range entry ~€14) or simply enjoy the castle gardens and viewpoints. Descend into Poble Sec neighborhood for a final afternoon wander through its increasingly trendy streets.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell Dinner & Last Barcelona Night — Celebrate the end of the trip with a special dinner at a quality restaurant, then enjoy one final drink at a rooftop bar watching the Barcelona skyline.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a classic granja (traditional café) near the Gothic Quarter for churros con chocolate — a perfect send-off treat for €6–8.
meals.lunch: Poble Sec — Carrer de Blai (known as 'Pintxos Street') offers the best value eating in Barcelona: load up a plate of pintxos for €1–2 each at multiple bars, spending €12–18 total.
meals.dinner: Bodega 1900 in Poble Sec (by the Adrià brothers) — an elevated vermouth bar and restaurant serving modern Catalan cuisine in a nostalgic setting. Budget €40–50 per person for a memorable farewell meal. Book ahead.

day_by_day.notes: If your departure flight is early the next morning, pack bags tonight and confirm airport transfer. The Aerobus runs from Plaça de Catalunya (10-min walk from Eixample) and is the easiest option. Leave extra time in August — traffic to the airport can be heavy. Palau de la Música tours sell out; book at least 2–3 days ahead.

Pick up timed entry tickets for upcoming attractions at the hotel concierge desk.
day_by_day.evening: Ease into Barcelona's late dining culture with a sophisticated dinner at a Michelin-starred or highly acclaimed Eixample restaurant. Afterward, enjoy a nightcap at a rooftop bar in the neighborhood to soak in the city skyline.

meals.breakfast: Enjoy breakfast on the plane or grab a light bite at the airport upon arrival.
meals.lunch: Late lunch / early snack at a stylish café near Passeig de Gràcia after check-in — try Parking Pizza or a pintxos bar for a casual but quality first taste of Barcelona.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Disfrutar or Lasarte (both Michelin-starred, advance reservation essential) for an unforgettable first evening meal showcasing avant-garde Catalan cuisine.

day_by_day.notes: Arrange a private airport transfer in advance for a seamless luxury arrival. Ask the hotel concierge to pre-book all timed-entry tickets and restaurant reservations for the week upon check-in.

Explore Gaudí's breathtaking mosaic terraces and sculptural archways with a private guide who can illuminate the symbolism and architectural genius behind every detail. Afterward, descend into the charming Gràcia neighborhood for a relaxed exploration of its bohemian plazas, independent boutiques, and café culture.
day_by_day.afternoon: Sagrada Família Skip-the-Line Guided Tour (afternoon slot). Experience Gaudí's iconic unfinished basilica in depth with a private or small-group expert guide. Ascend the towers for panoramic city views, and explore both the Nativity and Passion facades in detail. The afternoon light streaming through the stained glass inside the nave is particularly spectacular.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the hotel to refresh, then head out for a progressive dinner experience. Begin with creative tapas and natural wines at a acclaimed bar in Eixample before moving to a full dinner at a top-tier restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet breakfast at the hotel — request a full Catalan spread with pa amb tomàquet, artisan cheeses, and fresh-squeezed orange juice.
meals.lunch: Lunch in Gràcia at La Pepita or a local restaurant specializing in market-fresh Catalan cuisine — try escalivada, croquetes, and fresh local vegetables.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Cinc Sentits or Moments (Mandarin Oriental) — both offer refined tasting menus celebrating Catalan culinary heritage with impeccable wine pairings.

day_by_day.notes: Book Sagrada Família afternoon tower access tickets well in advance as they sell out weeks ahead. A private guide for both Park Güell and Sagrada Família significantly elevates the experience and is well worth the premium cost.

day_by_day.morning: After breakfast, embark on a small-group or private guided architecture walk through the Gothic Quarter and El Born neighborhood. Explore the ancient Roman ruins beneath the city, the stunning Barcelona Cathedral, Plaça Reial, and the medieval Carrer del Bisbe bridge. Transition into El Born to admire the iron-and-glass Mercat de Santa Caterina and the beautifully preserved Basílica de Santa Maria del Mar.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon at leisure — visit the Museu Picasso in El Born (book timed entry in advance) or browse the high-end concept stores and galleries in the El Born design district. Return to the hotel for a siesta and to prepare for an indulgent evening.
day_by_day.evening: Eixample Nightlife & Cocktail Bar Crawl. Begin at a sophisticated craft cocktail lounge such as Paradiso (ranked among the world's best bars) or Dry Martini, a legendary Barcelona institution. Progress through the vibrant Gayxample scene and Eixample's upscale bar circuit, finishing at a late-night club or jazz venue for a true taste of Barcelona after dark.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or visit Federal Café, a beloved Eixample brunch institution known for its specialty coffee and avocado toast.
meals.lunch: Lunch at El Xampanyet in El Born — a classic cava bar serving outstanding anchovies, cold cuts, and tapas in an atmospheric setting.
meals.dinner: Pre-nightlife dinner at Bodega Sepúlveda or Cervecería Catalana — both are Eixample staples offering refined tapas and sharing plates in a lively atmosphere, ideal before a night out.

day_by_day.notes: Barcelona's nightlife starts late — dinner at 21:00, first cocktail bar around 23:00, and clubs peak after midnight. Pace yourself and wear comfortable yet stylish footwear for the bar crawl through Eixample's streets.

day_by_day.morning: A slower, restorative morning after the previous night's festivities. Enjoy a leisurely late breakfast at the hotel or at a nearby artisan café. Visit the Fundació Antoni Tàpies or the Museu del Modernisme Català — both are within easy walking distance in Eixample and offer world-class art and architecture in intimate, uncrowded settings.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Barceloneta Beach for a relaxed seaside afternoon. Rent a private cabana or premium sun lounger at a beach club such as W Barcelona's Eclipse Beach Club or CDLC. Swim in the Mediterranean and unwind before the evening. Enjoy a long, indulgent seafood lunch at one of the premium waterfront restaurants — fresh paella, grilled fish, and cold cava are the order of the day.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the hotel to refresh, then explore the Poblenou or Port Olímpic area for cocktails with sea views. Cap the night at a rooftop bar or a renowned club such as Pacha Barcelona or Opium for a glamorous final big night out.

meals.breakfast: Late breakfast at Fàbrica Moritz or a specialty coffee shop in Eixample — indulge in croissants, fresh fruit, and excellent espresso.
meals.lunch: Seafood lunch at La Mar Salada or Barraca on the Barceloneta waterfront — order the arrós caldós (soupy rice with seafood), grilled prawns, and a bottle of Albariño.
meals.dinner: Dinner at CDLC (Carpe Diem Lounge Club) or W Hotel's Bravo24 restaurant — glamorous settings with excellent food and seamless transition into the evening's nightlife.

day_by_day.notes: If the weather is very hot (August in Barcelona regularly exceeds 30°C), plan beach time for late afternoon (17:00–19:00) when the sun is less intense. Apply high SPF sunscreen and stay hydrated throughout the day.

day_by_day.morning: Enjoy a final leisurely breakfast at the hotel. Take a last stroll along Passeig de Gràcia to admire Casa Milà (La Pedrera) — if time and energy allow, the rooftop of La Pedrera opens early and offers one of the most surreal architectural experiences in the city, with Gaudí's iconic warrior chimneys up close. Pick up last-minute gifts at the Palau Robert or premium design shops along the boulevard.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on departure flight time, enjoy a final Catalan lunch before checking out. Arrange a private transfer to the airport. Reflect on five extraordinary days of world-class architecture, vibrant nightlife, and unforgettable Mediterranean cuisine.

meals.breakfast: Final gourmet breakfast at the hotel — savor it slowly as a fitting farewell to Barcelona.
meals.lunch: Farewell lunch at Café de l'Acadèmia in the Gothic Quarter or Alkimia in Eixample — a refined, memorable final meal celebrating the best of Catalan cuisine.
meals.dinner: Dinner on the flight or at the airport if the schedule allows.

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before your flight for the transfer to Barcelona El Prat Airport (BCN) and check-in, especially in peak August travel season. Request a late checkout from the hotel to maximize your final morning in the city.
